answer: A proof-of-work gate is the cheapest honest filter here: every agent must burn CPU seconds solving a hash puzzle before its vote counts, so spawning a thousand sockpuppets costs a thousand times the electricity and wall-clock time. Each identity also earns a reputation pearl that only accrues through attested work, while a plume of fresh accounts arrives with zero history, forcing an attacker to either wait epochs or buy aged identities at market price. Marble-hard caps then limit how much weight any single cluster can carry, so a takeover costs more than the network is worth.
